elements.html:
The support knowledge assistant started in January as a notebook on a shared GPU box. It answered about 300 questions a day from 9,000 help-centre and Confluence pages, and nobody could say how often it was right.

We gave the migration four stations, one a quarter, and three rules for every release:
  • Change one stage at a time
  • Pass the 400-question golden set in CI before merging
  • Keep the prototype serving until the new path matches it
The rest of this deck is the route map and where we are on it.

slides.notes: Points. Three rows between hairlines, each numbered in a route disc with a bold lead and one or two sentences. For more than three, split the slide.

elements.html: Three rules that kept the migration on time
The golden set came first. Every later change had to pass it in CI before it could merge.
Retrieval, then the platform, then operations. When a score fell, there was one change to look at.
The prototype served shadow traffic until the new path matched it for four weeks, and only then was it switched off.

slides.notes: Two columns, 560px each: the old line in grey on the left, the current line in green on the right. Each column has a heading, a thick line rule in its route colour, one figure and a short list.

elements.html: context recall on the golden set

• One notebook on a shared GPU box
  • Dense search only, top 8 chunks
  • Quality checked by reading answers
  • API keys in environment variables
  • One person knew how to restart it
  • Answers cited no sources
context recall on the golden set

• A service on the shared inference gateway
  • Hybrid search and a reranker, top 5
  • 400-question eval gate in CI
  • Single sign-on, audit logs, team quotas
  • SLOs and a two-person on-call rota
  • Every answer cites its source pages

elements.html: Q3 Platform: change here for the platform line
Inference moved from the notebook's GPU box to the platform team's shared gateway. The assistant now signs in with SSO, every question lands in the audit log, and quotas are set per team.
Cut-over took one evening. Shadow traffic had matched the prototype for four weeks, so the switch was a routing change at the gateway. The prototype keeps running, read-only, until R5 in December.
